item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
You notice the ironic situation in which I often find myself. It's a good question.
Writing and 'normal' thoughtful analysis is impossible without style A. I suppose mathematics and music are interesting exceptions. Perhaps math is more style A, while music is less style A. To communicate the observation I see, I must use style A. However, style B is what allows me to see what I see in the first place.
I neglected to mention in the post that style B is related to <a href="https://centertao.local/essays/correlations/" rel="nofollow">the correlations process</a>, a non-'normal' way of thought. Using correlations to ponder requires discerning similarities to the point of no return, or as close to that as one can get.
I do see style A 'owns' the human mind, by-and-large, which gets us into unnecessary difficulty (although, it keeps the 'pot stirred', which makes interesting drama). I use style A all the time for lighthearted thinking. The more serious the issue, and the more deeply I want to know, I must turn to style B. Both styles have utility. Style B is better for heavy deep understanding; style A is better for light surface understanding. Style B serves inner-self communication; style A serves external social communication. Like I said, it's an ironic situation!
Ignorance of the trap which style A can easily become is humanity's problem. The more clever and technological we become, the more serious this may be. While style A has been with us ever since we began to think, I don't imagine it was much of a problem until after the agricultural revolution (10,000 b.c.e.) when we lost the protective influences of tribal (hunter gatherer) life.

item.title: By: Dave
item.dc:creator: Dave
item.description: You seem to prefer style B even as you analyze the situation using style A. Is this a reaction to the overemphasis of style A in the world around you or is this a statement that B is actually better in your conception?
